title: A register with many names
description:
Model one x64 general-purpose register and the rules for writing its smaller parts. Write the class `Register`:

- `get64()`, `get32()`, `get16()`, `get8()` return the low 64, 32, 16 or 8 bits (as unsigned values).
- `set64(v)` replaces all 64 bits.
- `set32(v)` writes the low 32 bits **and clears the upper 32**, as the processor does.
- `set16(v)` writes the low 16 bits and leaves the other 48 unchanged.
- `set8(v)` writes the low 8 bits and leaves the other 56 unchanged.

Values passed to the smaller setters may have extra high bits: only the bits that fit are used.

```
Register r; r.set64(0xFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFF);
r.set8(7);    // get64() = 0xFFFFFFFFFFFFFF07
r.set16(300); // get64() = 0xFFFFFFFFFFFF012C
r.set32(5);   // get64() = 5
```
hints: Reading a part is a cast to the smaller unsigned type, which keeps only the low bits.
Writing 16 or 8 bits: clear those bits in the stored value with `& ~mask`, then OR in the new bits `& mask`. Writing 32 bits is different: the whole value becomes just the new low 32 bits.
lessonTitle: Registers and the Shape of an Instruction
